title: Understand filters and read cost
summary: A FilterExpression removes items after DynamoDB reads the key-matching data.
introduction: A FilterExpression removes items after DynamoDB reads the key-matching data. Your task: Explain why a filter can return few rows after reading more.
learningObjectives: Explain why a filter can return few rows after reading more.
Explain the example for understand filters and read cost

blocks.text: A FilterExpression removes items after DynamoDB reads the key-matching data. It does not make that earlier read work disappear.

Use DynamoDB Local and the AWS CLI or SDK in a separate practice project. Point every command at http://localhost:8000. Low-level JSON examples show request bodies; provide them to the matching CLI command or SDK method.
Read the code step by step

items: `KeyConditionExpression` uses the table or index keys to select a partition and, optionally, a sort-key range.
`ConditionExpression` checks the current item as part of the write, so a failed condition prevents the change.
`ExpressionAttributeNames` maps placeholders such as #reader to actual field names in the request expression.

blocks.text: Only matching items with pages at least 50 are returned, but the query reads the partition candidates first.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: A selective filter on a huge partition can still be expensive. Design a suitable key or index for important access patterns.
